- Interstitial lung disease (e.g., smoking-related ILD, RB-ILD, or UIP — requires HRCT correlation)  
- Sarcoidosis (less likely without bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, elevated ACE, or skin/eye involvement)  
- Early COPD with atypical presentation (but normal spirometry argues against significant airflow obstruction)  

No evidence yet of hypercalcemia, anemia, or leukocytosis to suggest paraneoplastic syndrome or active infection. Definitive diagnosis hinges on imaging interpretation and bronchoscopic pathology.

All other differentials (TB, sarcoid, ILD) are plausible but require positive supporting evidence (e.g., nodules + cavitation, bilateral hilar adenopathy, reticular opacities on HRCT); none are supported by current data.

[DIAGNOSIS]
